SMTO-DB-0011 — The saved database connection is missing its address

GUID: 89a8e7a2-af06-42cd-b035-3e220f4e032c
Slug: database-profile-incomplete
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • The saved database entry SMTO picked doesn't include the full address of the database: its host, port or database name is empty. Nothing was sent to your database.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel to see which parts are missing: host, port or database name. SMTO lists exactly which parts of the address it couldn't find.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the database entry, open the Value tab, select Reveal & edit value, fill in the missing parts, then select Save. SMTO needs all three parts to know which database server, and which database on it, to use.
  3. If you have another entry for the same database that is complete, type @ in the conversation and pick that one instead. A complete entry already has the full address SMTO needs.

What success looks like

  • SMTO connects to the database and answers your question.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the database, and ask for the database's host, port and database name. Typing a password won't fix this; the address is what's missing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Database profile is missing a required host, port or database name (dbname), so the connection was refused before credentials were checked or anything was executed.

What this means

  • connection_error finds an empty host, port or dbname in the resolved database profile before checking credential completeness. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • connection_error finds an empty host, port or dbname in the resolved database profile before checking credential completeness.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect which public connection identity field is absent; changing a password cannot supply a database address.

How to fix it

  • connection_error() reports the missing fields in missing_fields (host, port and/or dbname, including aliases such as hostname, server, database, db or database_name). Fill those in the Parameter Store entry's value, or select a different, complete database profile. Supplying user or password through auth_values cannot change the target and does not fix a missing host or database name.
  • Correct or select a configured Database profile with the missing connection identity fields. Supplying credentials does not correct a missing host or database name.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended profile has all required address fields and resolves to the expected database.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
